sentences.text: Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Code') has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing the impugned order dated 29th August, 2013 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, Hamirpur, District Hamirpur, H.P, in Complaint No.27-III/2007/118- 1-2009, whereby application under Section 20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, has been allowed and the petitioner has been ordered to be summoned and impleaded as accused No.2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, Hamirpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
2.

Brief facts giving rise to the present petition are that respondent No.1/Food Inspector, Hamirpur,
filed a complaint under .
Section 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act')

in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur, the same was assigned to the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, of Hamirpur, for disposal in accordance with law.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Court No.II, of Hamirpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is alleged in the complaint that on 5th March, 2007 at about 1:00 pm, respondent rt No.1/Food Inspector, inspected the shop of respondent No.2 and found ten original sealed packets of "Vanaspati Ghee" for sale to the General Public with mark DO Khajoor manufactured by Bhatinda Chemical Limited, Hazi Road, Bhatinda, weighing 1000 ml.
Thereafter, respondent No.1 associated the witnesses of sample process to take the sample of Ghee from respondent No.2 and issued notice on Form No.7, which was duly signed by respondent No.2.

It is further alleged that respondent No.1 purchased three original sealed packets each of 100 ml;. of "Vansapati Ghee" from respondent No.2 on payment of `189/-, against proper receipt issued by respondent No.2 and signed by the witnesses.
After completing all the codal formalities, the sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst, Kandaghat, who found the same to be adulterated, as per the report submitted by him.
Respondent No.1 obtained sanction from the competent authority to initiate the prosecution against respondent No.2.
The complaint was filed on 19th November, 2007 and on receipt thereof, notice was issued to .

respondent No.2, who moved an application under Section 13 (ii) of the Act, for sending the sealed sample which was sealed by Food Inspector and sent to the Public Analyst, Mysore, the report was received by the learned Court, same was different from the report of submitted by the Public Analyst, Kandaghat.
Notice of Accusation was put to respondent No.2/accused, who pleaded not guilty and rt claimed trial.

After leading the prosecution evidence, defence was recorded and an application under Section 20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, was moved on behalf of respondent No.2 for impleading present petitioner, as co-accused, on the ground that he had purchased the same from the present petitioner.
The application was not contested by the complainant.

The same was allowed, vide order dated 29.8.2013 and the petitioner was impleaded,
as co-accused, with respondent No.2.
3.

The petitioner has assailed his impleadment on the ground that the learned Court below has not applied proper mind and not come to the conclusion after going through the evidence and conducting proper inquiry that the petitioner is a necessary party.

M/S Himachal Trading Company vs State Of H.P & Others on 1 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113106546/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the record in detail.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has argued that the petitioner was neither necessary nor proper party, .
as there is no evidence against the petitioner and the impugned order passed by the learned Court below is liable to be set aside.

He has further argued that the learned Court below has not conducted any inquiry with respect to the involvement of the of petitioner and simply made petitioner, as accused, vide order dated 29.8.2013.

6. rt Learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 has argued that there is no illegality and irregularity in the impugned order passed by the learned Court below,
therefore, the present petition is not maintainable.

7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.3 has argued that there was ample evidence on record to implead the petitioner/applicant as respondent, as he has sold the sealed material to the petitioner and the impugned order passed by the learned Court below suffers from no illegality.
8. In rebuttal, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has argued that the petitioner has not manufactured the material, which is evident from the record.
9. After taking into consideration the law as cited by this Hon'ble High Court in Krishan Kumar Jain vs. State of H.P and another, 1997 (1), SLC, 363, wherein it has been held as under:

entities.text: Krishan Kumar Jain vs. State of H.P and another, 1997 (1), SLC, 363
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
" 3. At the very outset, it may be stated that the impugned order passed by the learned Magistrate summoning the petitioner as co-accused under Section .
20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is bad and cannot be sustained.

It is well settled that before a person can be summoned under Section 20-A, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the Court has to hold an inquiry to find out whether prima facie the article of food of which the sample was taken by the Food Inspector was of purchased from the manufacturer, dealer or supplier alleged by the person making the application.
5. As stated above, in the present case no rt inquiry was conducted.
The impugned order, therefore, cannot be sustained.
The present petition is allowed.

The impugned order is set aside and the learned Magistrate shall proceed to dispose of the application under Section 20-A, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act afresh in accordance with law, and if satisfied that the petitioner is also connected with the commission of the offence as manufacturer, distributor or dealer, may implead him M/S Himachal Trading Company vs State Of H.P & Others on 1 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113106546/
3 as co-accused alongwith respondent No.2."
10.

entities.text: Himachal Trading Company vs State Of H.P & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After going through the entire record, this Court finds that the learned Court below has just ordered the issuance of notice to the present petitioner after allowing application under Section 20 (A) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The impugned order dated 29.8.2013 reads as under:
"Reply to application under Section 20 (A) of PFA Act, 1954.
Copy supplied.
Considered.
As per reply filed by the complainant, it has been stated that he has got no objection in case application is allowed.

Accordingly, after perusal of record,
statement of witnesses and that complainant has no objection the present application is allowed and M/s Himachal Trading Co; Near Bus Stand, Hamirpur, is necessary made as an .
accused in the present case.
Let notice be issued to newly impleaded accused for 11.9.2013."
11. In the instant case, the inquiry has not been conducted as required under Law.

The learned Court below has to first satisfy of with respect to the involvement of present petitioner and pass order with r e s p e c t t o s a t i s f a c t i o n o f t h e C o u r t q u a t h e i n v o l v e m e n t o f p e t i t i o n e r r t a s dealer/supplier/manufacturer/distributor.

So, applying the law as stated hereinabove, the impugned order is set aside and the learned Magistrate is ordered to dispose of the application under Section 20 (A) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 afresh in accordance with law and if satisfied that the petitioner is also connected with the commission of the offence as manufacturer, distributor or dealer, petitioner may be impleaded as co-accused alongwith respondent No.2.
Parties are directed to appear before the learned trial Court on 29th September, 2016.
12. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of, so also the pending application (s), if any.

1st September, 2016 (Chander Bhusan Barowalia)
